14:1.sourceText: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν Ἰκονίῳ κατὰ τὸ αὐτὸ εἰσελθεῖν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν συναγωγὴν τῶν Ἰουδαίων καὶ λαλῆσαι οὕτως ὥστε πιστεῦσαι Ἰουδαίων τε καὶ Ἑλλήνων πολὺ πλῆθος.
14:1.targetText: And it came to pass in Iconium, that they entered together into the synagogue of the Jews, and spoke, so that there believed a great multitude of both Jews and Greeks;

groups.note: The actual κατὰ τὸ αὐτό forms the together expression; the same adjective is part of this adverbial constituent, not a personal themselves pronoun.
The actual entering infinitive is rendered as the finite that-they-entered complement of it-came-to-pass; that is not a separately printed Greek conjunction here.
The actual οὕτως and ὥστε jointly give the manner/result connection, condensed as so that; both real words are retained in this constituent.
The actual πιστεῦσαι is an aorist active infinitive, rendered finite there believed in the English result clause; there is an English clause-frame word, not a printed Greek location adverb.

14:2.sourceText: οἱ δὲ ἀπειθήσαντες Ἰουδαῖοι ἐπήγειραν καὶ ἐκάκωσαν τὰς ψυχὰς τῶν ἐθνῶν κατὰ τῶν ἀδελφῶν.
14:2.targetText: and the unbelieving Jews stirred up and made the souls of the nations evil against the brothers;

groups.note: The actual ἀπειθήσαντες is an aorist active participle of ἀπειθέω, refusing belief or compliance, rendered unbelieving; pinned TR has a present participle of that same lemma. It is not replaced by an ἀπιστέω occurrence. Primary dictionary: https://www.billmounce.com/greek-dictionary/apeitheo .

The actual κακόω is one harming or embittering verb, rendered made ... evil; no independent making verb or evil adjective is printed in this predicate. Primary lexical entry specifically includes embitter at Acts14:2: https://www.billmounce.com/greek-dictionary/kakoo .

14:3.sourceText: ἱκανὸν μὲν οὖν χρόνον διέτριψαν παρρησιαζόμενοι ἐπὶ τῷ Κυρίῳ τῷ μαρτυροῦντι ἐπὶ τῷ λόγῳ τῆς χάριτος αὐτοῦ, διδόντι σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα γίνεσθαι διὰ τῶν χειρῶν αὐτῶν.
14:3.targetText: [for a] long time, indeed, therefore, they abided speaking boldly in the LORD, who is testifying to the word of His grace, and granting signs and wonders to come to pass through their hands.

groups.note: The actual accusative time noun gives duration, rendered for a ... time; the bracketed for a does not require a separately printed Greek preposition or indefinite article.
The actual ἐπί with the Lord is rendered in the Lord; its source preposition remains ἐπί, not an invented ἐν.
The actual γίνεσθαι is the happening/becoming infinitive, rendered to come to pass; it is not a printed coming verb.

unmappedSource.reason: The article under their hands is not separately expressed.

unmappedTarget.reason: The pinned TR includes an additional καί before granting; it is absent from pinned N1904.

14:4.sourceText: ἐσχίσθη δὲ τὸ πλῆθος τῆς πόλεως, καὶ οἱ μὲν ἦσαν σὺν τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις, οἱ δὲ σὺν τοῖς ἀποστόλοις.
14:4.targetText: And the multitude of the city was divided, and some were with the Jews, and some with the apostles,

groups.note: The actual article and μέν form the first side of the distributive contrast, rendered some; the contrasting article with δέ supplies the second some clause.

14:5.sourceText: ὡς δὲ ἐγένετο ὁρμὴ τῶν ἐθνῶν τε καὶ Ἰουδαίων σὺν τοῖς ἄρχουσιν αὐτῶν ὑβρίσαι καὶ λιθοβολῆσαι αὐτούς,
14:5.targetText: and when there was a purpose both of the nations and of the Jews with their rulers to mistreat [them], and to stone them,

groups.note: The actual ἐγένετο is a happened/arose predicate, rendered there was; it is not an occurrence of the Greek be lemma.
The actual ὁρμή is an impulse or attempt noun, rendered purpose; it is not the different πρόθεσις purpose noun. Primary lexical entry: https://www.billmounce.com/greek-dictionary/horme .
The one actual object αὐτούς supplies the same people threatened by both coordinated mistreating and stoning. English repeats them for the two actions; no second source object pronoun is invented.

unmappedSource.reason: The article under their rulers is not separately expressed.

14:6.sourceText: συνιδόντες κατέφυγον εἰς τὰς πόλεις τῆς Λυκαονίας Λύστραν καὶ Δέρβην καὶ τὴν περίχωρον·
14:6.targetText: they having become aware, fled to the cities of Lycaonia, Lystra, and Derbe, and the surrounding region,

groups.note: The actual συνιδόντες is an understanding/perceiving participle, expressed having become aware with its same plural participants. It does not print an independent becoming verb.
The actual περίχωρον is a substantival surrounding adjective, both tags A-ASF, rendered surrounding region; no independent region noun is printed.

14:7.targetText: and there they were proclaiming good news.

groups.note: The actual κἀκεῖ contracts and there; both English words belong to this one printed source word.
The actual good-news-proclaiming participle and the written were verb form the ongoing predicate; news is not an independent source noun.

14:8.sourceText: Καί τις ἀνὴρ ἀδύνατος ἐν Λύστροις τοῖς ποσὶν ἐκάθητο, χωλὸς ἐκ κοιλίας μητρὸς αὐτοῦ ὃς οὐδέποτε περιεπάτησεν.
14:8.targetText: And a certain man in Lystra, impotent in the feet, was sitting, being lame from the womb of his mother—who never had walked;

groups.note: The actual περιεπάτησεν is aorist active in both pinned N1904 analyses, rendered English past-perfect had walked. The pinned TR has a pluperfect walking form; the actual N1904 form is not changed to that reading.

unmappedTarget.reason: The pinned TR includes ὑπάρχων with the lame description, absent from N1904; the actual N1904 lame adjective does not independently supply this being predicate.

14:9.sourceText: οὗτος ἤκουεν τοῦ Παύλου λαλοῦντος· ὃς ἀτενίσας αὐτῷ καὶ ἰδὼν ὅτι ἔχει πίστιν τοῦ σωθῆναι,
14:9.targetText: this one was hearing Paul speaking, who, having steadfastly beheld him, and having seen that he has faith to be saved,

groups.note: The actual article and passive infinitive form the articular-infinitive complement, rendered to be saved; the article is not detached onto a bare English to without its verbal head.

unmappedSource.reason: The article before Paul is not separately expressed.

14:10.sourceText: εἶπεν μεγάλῃ φωνῇ Ἀνάστηθι ἐπὶ τοὺς πόδας σου ὀρθός. καὶ ἥλατο καὶ περιεπάτει.
14:10.targetText: said with a loud voice, “Stand up on your feet upright”; and he was springing and walking,

groups.note: The actual dative voice noun gives the means, rendered with a loud voice without a separately printed Greek with preposition.

The actual ἥλατο is aorist with both tags V-ADI-3S; the pinned TR instead has imperfect ἥλλετο behind English was springing. The common springing head is retained without claiming an imperfect N1904 form.
The actual περιεπάτει is a finite imperfect walking predicate; English uses walking with its shared was frame rather than a source participle.

unmappedSource.reason: The article under your feet is not separately expressed.

14:11.sourceText: οἵ τε ὄχλοι ἰδόντες ὃ ἐποίησεν Παῦλος ἐπῆραν τὴν φωνὴν αὐτῶν Λυκαονιστὶ λέγοντες Οἱ θεοὶ ὁμοιωθέντες ἀνθρώποις κατέβησαν πρὸς ἡμᾶς,
14:11.targetText: and the multitudes having seen what Paul did, lifted up their voice in the speech of Lycaonia, saying, “The gods, having become like men, came down to us”;

groups.note: The actual Λυκαονιστί is one language adverb, in Lycaonian, rendered in the speech of Lycaonia; speech and the place-name are not independent source nouns.
The actual ὁμοιωθέντες is a passive aorist likeness-making participle, rendered having become like; no separate Greek becoming verb is printed.

unmappedSource.reason: The article under their voice is not separately expressed.

14:12.sourceText: ἐκάλουν τε τὸν Βαρνάβαν Δία, τὸν δὲ Παῦλον Ἑρμῆν, ἐπειδὴ αὐτὸς ἦν ὁ ἡγούμενος τοῦ λόγου.
14:12.targetText: they were also calling Barnabas Zeus, and Paul Hermes, since he was the leader in speaking.

groups.note: The actual ἡγούμενος is a nominalized leading participle, rendered leader; it is not an independent Greek leader noun.
The actual genitive article/λόγου speech construction is recast as in speaking; its source stays the λόγος noun, not an invented speaking verb.

unmappedSource.reason: The articles before Barnabas and Paul are not separately expressed.

14:13.sourceText: ὅ τε ἱερεὺς τοῦ Διὸς τοῦ ὄντος πρὸ τῆς πόλεως, ταύρους καὶ στέμματα ἐπὶ τοὺς πυλῶνας ἐνέγκας, σὺν τοῖς ὄχλοις ἤθελεν θύειν.
14:13.targetText: And the priest of the Zeus that is before their city, having brought oxen and garlands to the porches, wished to sacrifice with the multitudes,

groups.note: The actual ὄντος is a present participle of be and supplies the English is; this is a real written being predicate rather than an unwritten copula.

unmappedSource.reason: The article under their city is not separately expressed.

unmappedTarget.reason: The pinned TR includes an additional αὐτῶν with city, absent from N1904; no city-owner pronoun is invented.

14:14.sourceText: ἀκούσαντες δὲ οἱ ἀπόστολοι Βαρνάβας καὶ Παῦλος, διαρρήξαντες τὰ ἱμάτια ἑαυτῶν ἐξεπήδησαν εἰς τὸν ὄχλον, κράζοντες
14:14.targetText: and having heard, the apostles Barnabas and Paul, having torn their garments, sprung into the multitude, crying

groups.note: The actual ἑαυτῶν is the reflexive genitive referring to the garment-tearing agents, rendered their; it is not a different nonreflexive αὐτῶν occurrence.

unmappedSource.reason: The article under their garments is not separately expressed.

14:15.sourceText: καὶ λέγοντες Ἄνδρες, τί ταῦτα ποιεῖτε; καὶ ἡμεῖς ὁμοιοπαθεῖς ἐσμεν ὑμῖν ἄνθρωποι, εὐαγγελιζόμενοι ὑμᾶς ἀπὸ τούτων τῶν ματαίων ἐπιστρέφειν ἐπὶ θεὸν ζῶντα, ὃς ἐποίησεν τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν καὶ τὴν θάλασσαν καὶ πάντα τὰ ἐν αὐτοῖς·
14:15.targetText: and saying, “Men, why do you do these things? And we are similar-feeling men with you, proclaiming good news to you, to turn to the living God from these vanities, who made the heaven, and the earth, and the sea, and all the things in them;

groups.note: The actual ὁμοιοπαθεῖς is a single shared-feeling/experience adjective, rendered similar-feeling; it does not contain an independently printed feeling verb.
The actual accusative ὑμᾶς is the gospel-recipient complement, rendered to you without a separately printed to preposition.
The actual ματαίων is a substantival vain adjective, rendered vanities; it is not the different ματαιότης abstract noun.

unmappedSource.reason: The article under these vanities is not separately expressed.

14:16.sourceText: ὃς ἐν ταῖς παρῳχημέναις γενεαῖς εἴασεν πάντα τὰ ἔθνη πορεύεσθαι ταῖς ὁδοῖς αὐτῶν·
14:16.targetText: who in the past generations permitted all the nations to go on in their ways,

groups.note: The actual παρῳχημέναις is a gone-by perfect participle, rendered past; its source remains that verbal form rather than an independent past adjective.
The actual dative article/ways complement is rendered in ... ways, retaining its nominal head rather than assigning bare in to the article alone.

14:17.sourceText: καίτοι οὐκ ἀμάρτυρον αὑτὸν ἀφῆκεν ἀγαθουργῶν, οὐρανόθεν ὑμῖν ὑετοὺς διδοὺς καὶ καιροὺς καρποφόρους, ἐμπιπλῶν τροφῆς καὶ εὐφροσύνης τὰς καρδίας ὑμῶν.
14:17.targetText: though, indeed, He did not leave Himself without witness, doing good—giving rains to us from Heaven, and fruitful seasons, filling our hearts with food and gladness”;

groups.note: The actual καίτοι is one concessive particle, rendered though indeed; the source has no separate γε particle printed, unlike the pinned TR καίτοιγε.
The actual ἀμάρτυρον is an unwitnessed/without-witness adjective, rendered without witness; it is not an independent negative preposition plus witness noun.
The actual αὑτόν has the reflexive breathing and is analyzed F-3ASM from ἑαυτοῦ in both source fields; it is not the unlike nonreflexive αὐτόν form.
The actual οὐρανόθεν is a single from-heaven adverb, rendered from Heaven; no independent Greek from preposition or heaven noun is printed there.
The actual genitive food noun gives filling content, rendered with food without a separately printed with preposition.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual ὑμῖν is second-person plural to you, whereas the pinned TR and English have first-person to us; the different recipients remain unpaired.
The article under the English possessive hearts expression is not separately expressed.
The actual ὑμῶν is second-person plural your, whereas the pinned TR and English have first-person our; the unlike possessors remain unpaired.

unmappedTarget.reason: The English follows the pinned TR first-person recipient instead of N1904 second-person to you.
The English follows pinned TR first-person our instead of N1904 second-person your.

14:18.sourceText: καὶ ταῦτα λέγοντες μόλις κατέπαυσαν τοὺς ὄχλους τοῦ μὴ θύειν αὐτοῖς.
14:18.targetText: and saying these things, they scarcely restrained the multitudes from sacrificing to them.

groups.note: The actual genitive articular infinitive includes μή under the restraining predicate. English renders this entire source construction from sacrificing without an additional English not; all three written source words remain together rather than dropping the negative.

14:19.sourceText: Ἐπῆλθαν δὲ ἀπὸ Ἀντιοχείας καὶ Ἰκονίου Ἰουδαῖοι, καὶ πείσαντες τοὺς ὄχλους καὶ λιθάσαντες τὸν Παῦλον ἔσυρον ἔξω τῆς πόλεως, νομίζοντες αὐτὸν τεθνηκέναι.
14:19.targetText: And there came there, from Antioch and Iconium, Jews, and they having persuaded the multitudes, and having stoned Paul, drew him outside of the city, having supposed him to be dead;

groups.note: The actual Jews noun names the same immediate persuading agents, resumed as English they; no additional subject pronoun is invented.

The actual named Paul is the patient both stoned and immediately dragged out. English resumes that same named patient as him with dragging; the later actual pronoun has its own separate supposed-dead role.
The actual νομίζοντες is a present supposing participle, rendered having supposed; no aorist source form is substituted.
The actual τεθνηκέναι is a perfect active infinitive of die, rendered to be dead as the resulting-state expression; it is not an εἰμί being infinitive.

unmappedSource.reason: The article before Paul is not separately expressed.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies this additional spatial there; no independent location adverb is printed in either pinned source here.

14:20.sourceText: κυκλωσάντων δὲ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτὸν ἀναστὰς εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὴν πόλιν. Καὶ τῇ ἐπαύριον ἐξῆλθεν σὺν τῷ Βαρνάβᾳ εἰς Δέρβην.
14:20.targetText: and the disciples having surrounded him, having risen he entered into the city, and on the next day he went forth with Barnabas to Derbe.

unmappedSource.reason: The article before Barnabas is not separately expressed.

14:21.sourceText: εὐαγγελιζόμενοί τε τὴν πόλιν ἐκείνην καὶ μαθητεύσαντες ἱκανοὺς ὑπέστρεψαν εἰς τὴν Λύστραν καὶ εἰς Ἰκόνιον καὶ εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν,
14:21.targetText: Having also proclaimed good news to that city, and having discipled many, they turned back to Lystra, and Iconium, and Antioch,

groups.note: The actual gospel-proclaiming participle is present, rendered English having proclaimed good news; no aorist source form is substituted.
The actual accusative article/city names the gospel-recipient city, rendered to ... city in the English indirect-recipient frame; the source case remains accusative.

Three actual εἰς prepositions introduce the three coordinated destinations. English states one shared to for that same list, so all three actual preposition identities jointly own the single English relation.

unmappedSource.reason: The article before Lystra is not separately expressed.

14:22.sourceText: ἐπιστηρίζοντες τὰς ψυχὰς τῶν μαθητῶν, παρακαλοῦντες ἐμμένειν τῇ πίστει, καὶ ὅτι διὰ πολλῶν θλίψεων δεῖ ἡμᾶς εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ.
14:22.targetText: confirming the souls of the disciples, exhorting to remain in the faith, and that it is required of us to enter into the Kingdom of God through many tribulations,

groups.note: The actual accusative ἡμᾶς is the personal subject of the entering infinitive, rendered of us under the English is-required frame; it is not a Greek genitive pronoun.

14:23.sourceText: χειροτονήσαντες δὲ αὐτοῖς κατ’ ἐκκλησίαν πρεσβυτέρους, προσευξάμενοι μετὰ νηστειῶν παρέθεντο αὐτοὺς τῷ Κυρίῳ εἰς ὃν πεπιστεύκεισαν.
14:23.targetText: and having appointed to them elders in every assembly by vote, having prayed with fastings, they commended them to the LORD in whom they had believed.

groups.note: The actual χειροτονέω is one appointing/electing verb, rendered by this translation having appointed by vote. There is no independently printed by preposition or vote noun in that predicate. Primary lexical range: https://www.billmounce.com/greek-dictionary/cheirotoneo .
The actual κατά is distributive with assembly, rendered in every assembly without a separate Greek every adjective.

14:24.sourceText: καὶ διελθόντες τὴν Πισιδίαν ἦλθον εἰς τὴν Παμφυλίαν,
14:24.targetText: And having passed through Pisidia, they came to Pamphylia,

unmappedSource.reason: The articles before Pisidia and Pamphylia are not separately expressed.

14:25.sourceText: καὶ λαλήσαντες ἐν Πέργῃ τὸν λόγον κατέβησαν εἰς Ἀτταλίαν,
14:25.targetText: and having spoken the word in Perga, they went down to Attalia,

14:26.sourceText: κἀκεῖθεν ἀπέπλευσαν εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν, ὅθεν ἦσαν παραδεδομένοι τῇ χάριτι τοῦ Θεοῦ εἰς τὸ ἔργον ὃ ἐπλήρωσαν.
14:26.targetText: and [from] there sailed to Antioch, from where they had been given by the grace of God for the work that they fulfilled;

groups.note: The actual κἀκεῖθεν contracts and from there; even the bracketed English from belongs to the real from-there adverb rather than an invented independent Greek preposition.
The actual imperfect were plus perfect passive entrusted/given participle form the periphrastic past-perfect expression rendered they had been given; there is no independent Greek had word.
The actual article/grace is dative, rendered by the grace in this translation; it is not a printed ὑπό agent preposition.

14:27.sourceText: Παραγενόμενοι δὲ καὶ συναγαγόντες τὴν ἐκκλησίαν, ἀνήγγελλον ὅσα ἐποίησεν ὁ Θεὸς μετ’ αὐτῶν, καὶ ὅτι ἤνοιξεν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν θύραν πίστεως.
14:27.targetText: and having come and gathered the assembly together, they declared as many things as God did with them, and that He opened a door of faith to the nations;

groups.note: The actual ὅσα is one neuter plural quantitative relative, expanded as many things as; no independent Greek thing noun or many adjective is printed.

unmappedSource.reason: The article before God is not separately expressed.

14:28.sourceText: διέτριβον δὲ χρόνον οὐκ ὀλίγον σὺν τοῖς μαθηταῖς.
14:28.targetText: and they abided there with the disciples [for] not a short time.

groups.note: The actual accusative time noun gives duration, expressed for ... a ... time. The bracketed for reflects this real duration construction without a separately printed Greek for preposition.

unmappedTarget.reason: The pinned TR has an additional ἐκεῖ place adverb, absent from N1904; no local source adverb is invented.
